title: astra-gi.toml, schema 1 (JSON projection)
description: A manifest as JSON, isomorphic to the TOML astra-game-launcher reads. Covers both the base sections GAME-INTEGRATION-MANIFEST.md already defines and the [integration.*] additions in manifest.md. additionalProperties:false mirrors exactly the sections astra-game-launcher's src/manifest.rs refuses an unknown key in (TOP_KEYS, TARGET_KEYS, FILES_KEYS, GAME_FILES_KEYS, LAUNCH_KEYS, CONFIG_WRITES_KEYS); [integration] itself stays open, because v0.3.1 reads it with no key check at all.

engineCode.description: spec/games/reserved.yaml engine_code_pattern. Reservation (the four built-ins, 'unknown', or a code already owned by another publisher) is an ingest-time fact, not a structural one, so it is not re-expressed as a schema enum.

integration.description: Metadata. v0.3.1 reads this table with no key check (src/manifest.rs:27-38), so additionalProperties stays true — a future [integration.*] table must be readable by today's client without a schema bump.

sdk.description: manifest.md §2.5. Metadata only; shown in Settings -> Developer, never on the install sheet.

integrationEngine.description: manifest.md §2.1. Present only on the foundation that owns this engine code. Its full astra.engine/1 grammar is normative in engine-descriptor-v1.md and validated by engine-descriptor-v1.schema.json; this is a structural placeholder so manifest.schema.json alone can confirm the table's presence and its schema tag.

integrationLoader.description: manifest.md §2.2. proxies and keep_if_present must be disjoint (loader-policy-conflict); that is a cross-field rule gi-probe enforces, not expressible as a plain JSON Schema constraint here.

integrationCapabilities.description: manifest.md §2.3. v1's only companion id is 'presentation'.

integrationFoundation.description: manifest.md §2.4. A claim only; ingest computes built_on{entry,version,verified} from digests.

integrationLink.description: manifest.md §2.6. Structural shape only; the message protocol and the restricted data-schema profile are normative in link-v1.md and its own schemas/ files.

context.description: manifest.md §2.6: the path of the context schema, held to link-v1.md §6's AI profile. Absent = the GI sends no context.

knowledge.description: manifest.md §2.6, link-v1.md §5 'Knowledge': the path of the knowledge folder in the zip. Requires knowledge_licence (semantic rule knowledge-without-licence).

knowledge_licence.description: manifest.md §2.6: the knowledge base's licence, an SPDX id or text; shown on the consent sheet.

tools.description: manifest.md §2.6: at most 16 tools, or 24 for a GI with a danger = "game" tool (semantic rule tools-over-16-without-game).

name.description: At most 32 characters, so game_<entryhash8>_<name> stays within 46 (link-v1.md §5 'Tools').

result.description: link-v1.md §5 'A tool's result': the path of the result schema, held to §6's AI profile. Required.

danger.description: link-v1.md §5 'Tool danger'. Absent = high; low and game are honoured only from a signed catalogue entry. game: an action in the player's own game, when they ask, in a world where they are alone (§5 'Actions in the game').

companion.description: link-v1.md §5 'Tools that act on her'. Absent = false.

stops.description: link-v1.md §5 'Actions in the game': the tool ends all of her game work. A GI with a game tool needs one, and it is low (semantic rules game-without-stop, stops-not-low). Absent = false.

name.description: link-v1.md §5 'Event words': the closed v1 list. work_ended only with a game tool and never speaks (semantic rule work-ended-misdeclared).

speaks.description: link-v1.md §5 'Speaking on her own'. Absent = false.

integrationContent.description: manifest.md §2.7. One entry per non-built-in asset this GI ships (its own animations, models, art or audio). Cross-entry rules a JSON Schema cannot express -- a path declared more than once, a content-typed file with no entry or an entry with no file, the HARD VRM licence gate -- are gi-probe check's and the catalogue ingest's job, not this schema's. maxItems 1024 is contract 6.13.0 §4.6's candidate bound (at most 1024 parts[]), enforced here so a manifest past it is refused before it ever reaches ingest.

integrationContentEntry.description: manifest.md §2.7. kind is restricted to the four GI content kinds. 'command' exists in the shared asset-rights rule (astra-ce's character-asset confirmation) but is never valid for a GI, so it is simply absent from this enum. licence is OPTIONAL (legal DRAFT-v3.md Part 6 G5): a .vrm part's real licence is read from the file itself, and the content check refuses E_CONTENT_LICENCE_UNDECLARED only when BOTH that reading fails or does not apply AND this key is absent -- see manifest.md §2.7.3.

path.description: relative, no '..' segment, no ':' (so a 'builtin:' reference can never read as a declared part). This is the part's id; uniqueness across entries is a semantic rule (gi-probe check / ingest), not expressible here.
